question: A current of 15 mA is flowing through an electronic device when the voltage across the device is 0.3 mV. The resistance of the device is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 mΩ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The current flowing through the device is **15 mA** (milliamperes), which is equal to 0.015 A (amperes).
 
• The voltage across the device is **0.3 mV** (millivolts), which is equal to 0.0003 V (volts).
 
• Using Ohm's Law, which states that **R = V/I**, we can calculate the resistance of the device.
 
• By substituting the values into the formula, we get **R = 0.0003 V / 0.015 A = 0.02 Ω = 20 mΩ**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law:**

 
 
• Ohm's Law is a fundamental principle in electronics and electrical engineering which states that the current flowing through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is given as **V = I * R**, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
• This law helps in determining one of the three values (voltage, current, resistance) if the other two values are known.
 
 
 
• **Resistance:**
 
 
• Resistance is a measure of the opposition to the flow of electric current in a conductor.
 
• The unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).
 
• Materials with high resistance require more voltage to push the same amount of current compared to materials with low resistance.
 
 
 
• **Current:**
 
 
• Electric current is the flow of electric charge in a conductor.
 
• The unit of current is the ampere (A).
 
• Current can be measured using instruments such as ammeters.
 
 
 
• **Voltage:**
 
 
• Voltage, also known as electric potential difference, is the difference in electric potential between two points.
 
• The unit of voltage is the volt (V).
 
• Voltage can be measured using instruments such as voltmeters.
